correctness.rationale: For each type the named lower and upper portions of the chain are an initial and final segment, giving unique interval [i,j] with 0<=i<=j<=n. Distinct incomparable realizations exist exactly when the discrete intervals intersect: failure gives a transitive old witness; success gives a valid finite two-point partial order and is realized by the random poset extension property. Every internal row equals left boundary row plus right boundary row minus the full interval row, producing a free integral kernel basis. On boundary vectors f,u_j,v_i, subtracting f makes the same-side Gram blocks zero and the cross block -1_{j<i}; adjacent differences turn it into -I_n, so a unimodular integer congruence gives [1] plus n hyperbolic planes and binomial(n,2) zeros. The basis transformation has determinant +-1 by unitriangular operations. All field ranks, integral Smith factors and real inertia follow; standard-library exact checks for 0<=n<=9 independently verify matrix congruence and for 0<=n<=5 check the full pair-extension transitivity criterion.

originality.rationale: The claim is the explicit integral congruence, primitive null basis, all-characteristic rank and inertia of the looped interval-intersection feasibility matrix. Two fully inspected nearby published results compute, respectively, scalar ordered-tuple counts over named poset chains and quantifier-rank-three elementary theory classes of loopless complete interval graphs. Neither implies an integer congruence for this form. Inspected 2011 random-poset reduct paper supplies incomparability and extension axioms, the 2013 interval-graph model-checking work treats FO decision complexity, and Billionnet (1986) treats matrix envelopes and interval graph profiles rather than Smith invariant factors. The remaining risk is an unindexed older equivalent interval-matrix congruence.
residual_risks: Older interval-graph adjacency-plus-identity or matrix-congruence literature might contain an unindexed equivalent general theorem. Searches are not historical uniqueness proofs.
The tensor/simple-graph reformulations were queried, but no comprehensive specialist bibliography or independent priority review was available.
A published matching structural result could be filed under integer quadratic forms or interval-order matrices, not named-type feasibility.

value.rationale: An existential binary relation on complete one-point types of a classical homogeneous structure naturally yields a quadratic-size Boolean matrix. Determining its integral bilinear-form class is not a scalar counting exercise: it gives a primitive, explicit null lattice, no finite cokernel torsion, all-characteristic rank stability and constant signature for every chain length. The boundary-only rank certificate explains exactly why a quadratic number of types supplies only linearly many independent feasibility profiles. The result is structural, uniform and potentially useful for understanding finite-parameter type relations; it is not just a small numerical improvement or a table recomputation.
